paragraphs: I moved to the region in September to [[enroll]] in a graduate program, and I needed a [[platform]] for my fieldwork. A community centre offered me a desk on condition that I [[supervise]] the evening homework room twice a week. It was a [[casual]] arrangement, never written into a [[contract]]. The building was a converted [[warehouse]] with a [[peculiar]] smell of chalk and oranges. The director, a woman of great [[wisdom]] and little patience, said the centre was [[independent]] but always short of money.

My study looked at [[prosocial]] and [[altruistic]] behaviour in [[adolescent]]s. We wanted to know whether kindness can be [[cultivate]]d, or whether it is a fixed [[figure]] in a [[sequence]] of development. The [[underlying|underlie]] question is simple: what makes a teenager [[sacrifice]] an afternoon for someone else? We had to [[acquire]] consent from every parent, which proved harder than the [[biology]]. The ethics committee asked us to [[certify]] that no child would be [[swamp]]ed by questionnaires. I had to [[acquaint]] myself with a dozen names on the first afternoon, and I forgot half of them by Friday.

We measured [[visual]] attention, heart rate and a [[binary]] choice: keep the money or share it. Every [[particle]] of data was [[encode]]d and stored on a server that no volunteer could open. The [[incidence]] of sharing was higher than the literature predicted, which was a small [[marvel]]. A [[deficiency]] in sleep, we found, could [[reduce]] generosity by half. Even a [[casual]] remark from a teacher seemed to [[affect]] the [[outcome]]. Each child had a [[switch]] to [[donate]] privately, which removed the pressure of [[surround]]ing eyes.

By November the numbers looked too good, and I began a [[cursory]] check of the files. A [[redundant]] column of entries turned out to have been copied by hand. The error [[implicate]]d a volunteer who had meant no harm, and I had to [[withhold]] my anger. The [[critical]] point was not the mistake but the habit that produced it. I decided to [[rethink]] the whole [[sequence]] and to [[impose]] a rule: every entry verified twice. [[Scrutiny]] of my own work was the hardest part, and I had to [[critique]] my [[profile]] as a careful researcher.

In December the city announced that the centre's building would be sold to a [[third-party]] developer. A 1972 [[charter]] protected the site, but the council's [[declaration]] of intent suggested otherwise. The plan would [[violate]] the charter, according to our lawyer, though the [[penalty]] for that was unclear. The council argued that the centre was [[inadequate]] for modern needs and that its costs were [[swell]]ing. The director called the decision [[cruel]] and [[unrepresentative]] of the neighbourhood. I was [[indignant]], but I had learned that anger is a poor [[substitute]] for a plan.

The public meeting was held in a [[chamber]] with bad lighting. A councillor [[administer]]ed the questions and [[indicate]]d that the vote was already decided. The meeting was [[chaos]] for twenty minutes until someone found the agenda. The mood turned when a [[caregiver]] asked who would look after the children if the centre closed. Her [[sentiment]] was shared by most of the room, and the [[current]] of opinion shifted within an hour. The council's [[mandate]] was to save money, but the [[merit]] of the centre was obvious to everyone there.

That winter the news was full of [[violence]]: a [[hostage]] case two towns away, a [[widespread]] fear of strangers. Coverage of a single [[incident]] can [[swell]] into a [[series]] of stories with no new facts. A single [[transgression]] can come to [[denote]] a whole generation, the university's [[chancellor]] warned. I tried to [[differentiate]] between a [[credible]] risk and a [[virtual]] one. Fear, I wrote in my notes, is easy to [[impose]] and hard to [[withstand]]. A [[critical]] reading of the coverage showed how quickly a [[particular]] case becomes a [[symbol]].

The teenagers decided to answer with a [[rap]] performance and a [[platform]] of their own. They wrote a [[biography]] of the centre in verse, listing the [[lineage]] of families who had passed through it. Their [[critique]] of the council was sharper than mine, and far more [[credible]] to the neighbours. They asked me to [[advise]] them on facts, and I had to [[select]] which numbers mattered. The performance [[emerge]]d from six weeks of argument and [[acquire]]d a life of its own. They [[perform]]ed in the square, and the [[conversation]] afterwards was [[inclusive]] in a way the council's never was.

In January a [[pension]] fund offered to [[finance]] the purchase of the building. The offer required a [[definite]] commitment and a [[transparent]] [[record]] of our accounts. A [[third-party]] auditor would [[certify]] the figures [[annually]]. The [[upside]] was obvious, but the [[deduction]] from our independence was not small. The director said she would rather [[remain]] poor than be [[indifferent]] to who paid. We had to [[employ]] an accountant to [[organize]] the files, and he was calmer than all of us.

By February I was [[swamp]]ed with teaching, data and letters. My [[mental]] state was poor, and I began to [[incline]] towards quitting. A [[caregiver]] at the centre noticed before I did. She said the [[advantage]] of a [[delicate]] constitution is that you learn to [[adjust]] early. She [[advised|advise]] me to cut my hours, which felt like a [[penalty]] at the time. I began to [[reflect]] on why I had [[suppose]]d I could do everything alone.

My friend studies [[biology]], and she says the [[nutrient]] cycle in a small pond is a [[marvel]] of [[nurture]]. Every organism is a [[channel]] for energy, and none of it is [[redundant]]. Under the microscope, the [[acute]] problem is never one organism but the balance between all of them. She said a [[deficiency]] in one [[nutrient]] can [[threaten]] a whole [[region]]. The [[universe]] of a pond, she insisted, is as complete as any other.

In March the first [[series]] of results was ready. The data [[indicate]]d that [[unselfishly]] helping others [[peak]]s at fifteen and then levels off. The [[figure]]s were [[adequate]] to support a modest paper, though not a [[tremendous]] claim. I [[emphasize]]d the limits of the sample, which was small and [[unrepresentative]]. The [[outcome]] was [[non-controversial]], which is a rare pleasure in this field.

In April the city offered a deal: the centre could stay if it [[sustain]]ed itself for three years. A [[charter]] amendment would [[secure]] the building, and a [[penalty]] clause would protect it from resale. The council's lawyers tried to [[impose]] conditions that would [[violate]] the spirit of the deal. We asked them to [[withstand]] the temptation to add footnotes and to publish the [[contract]] in full. Two [[affiliate]]d groups [[enlist]]ed volunteers, and the [[demand]] for places [[stretch]]ed the timetable. The whole [[affair]] taught me that a [[merge]]d budget is easier to defend than a promise.

A local paper ran a [[profile]] of the director, and the [[feedback]] was warm. But a rival column published a [[cursory]] [[critique]] that [[insult]]ed her age. The [[insult]] was [[peculiar]]: it accused her of [[sentiment]] rather than judgement. I wrote a reply that tried to [[defend]] her, and the editor cut it to two paragraphs. She became the [[recipient]] of an award she had never applied for. The episode [[impel]]led me to [[prioritize]] the centre over my own thesis for a while.

In June the centre signed a five-year [[contract]] with the city. The [[warehouse]] was [[decorate]]d with the teenagers' paintings, and the room where we met became a studio. My study was published in a small journal, and the [[feedback]] was kind. I [[realise]] (or [[realize]]) that the data could not show what mattered most. Kindness is not a [[symbol]] on a questionnaire; it is a habit built by [[nurture]]. The [[upside]] of such a year is that you [[marvel]] at how much a small place can [[sustain]], and I still [[admire]] the director enough to [[include]] her in every [[conversation]] about the study.
